cycleHistory.title: Cycle history
cycleHistory.subtitle: Each bar is one cycle. The mark shows how that cycle's ovulation was established, if it was.

doctorExport.title: Doctor export
doctorExport.body: Your cycle lengths, ovulation evidence, and BBT/strip readings — on one page for your appointment.

cycleInsights.footerDisclaimer: A cycle showing an ovulatory signature is not proof an egg was released, and a cycle without one is not a diagnosis. This page describes what your signals did, nothing more.

toast.noDataDesc: Log a few days first — the report needs something to summarise.
toast.errorDesc: Please try again in a moment.

fertilityCard.title: Fertility Signals
fertilityCard.emptyState: Log a morning temperature and an ovulation test in the Tracker and your chart will build here across the cycle.
fertilityCard.healthSyncNote: Synced from Health — informational only, not part of the read above.

cycleOverview.lateMessageLong: A week or more is worth looking into. If pregnancy is possible, a test will tell you more — otherwise consider checking in with a doctor.
cycleOverview.lateMessageShort: A few days either way is common. Stress, illness, travel and poor sleep can all shift a cycle.
cycleOverview.ovulationNotTypical: This cycle didn't show a typical ovulation pattern — common, usually not urgent, worth mentioning if it happens often.

cycleAnomaly.title: Cycles worth a second look
cycleAnomaly.subtitle: Flagged against your own cycle-length history, not a population average.
cycleAnomaly.longerBody: That's {{diff}} days longer than your personal average of {{mean}} days.
cycleAnomaly.shorterBody: That's {{diff}} days shorter than your personal average of {{mean}} days.
cycleAnomaly.likelyExplanation: You logged "{{tag}}" more than usual during this cycle — worth noting as a possible factor.
cycleAnomaly.footer: A cycle standing out from your own pattern isn't a diagnosis — just something to keep an eye on, or mention to a doctor if it keeps happening.

hormoneRhythm.title: Thermal & autonomic rhythm
hormoneRhythm.subtitle: Your skin temperature, resting heart rate, and HRV — signals known to shift after ovulation — combined into one trend across this cycle.
hormoneRhythm.risingNote: These signals have climbed later in this cycle — consistent with the post-ovulatory shift the same signals show around when temperature-based ovulation detection confirms a cycle.
hormoneRhythm.footer: Not a hormone measurement — wearables can't read estrogen or progesterone directly. This is a pattern derived from temperature and heart signals, shown so you can see how it moves across your own cycle.

pcosPatterns.title: PCOS patterns
pcosPatterns.subtitle: How often each pattern has shown up across your logged cycles, not just this one.
pcosPatterns.footer: Patterns in what your signals showed, not a diagnosis — worth mentioning to your doctor if they keep showing up.

pmosScore.title: PMOS-pattern check-in
pmosScore.subtitle: {{flagged}} of {{total}} assessable {{indicatorWord}} commonly discussed alongside PMOS show up in your logged patterns.
pmosScore.footer: Educational only — not a diagnosis or a risk score. PMOS is diagnosed clinically, usually with bloodwork and an ultrasound. Worth bringing this up with a doctor if it resonates, not something to act on alone.

cycleTrendChart.title: BBT & test-strip trend
cycleTrendChart.subtitle: Each cycle's peak reading, side by side — not the daily chart above, which is this cycle only.
